🚨🚨BREAKING UPDATES 🚨 

🇦🇺 Muslim Hero Who Stopped Sydney Attack Gets Hospital Visit from Rabbi's Family

On a Sunday night at Bondi Beach, two gunmen opened fire on a Hanukkah celebration. 15 people died, including Rabbi Eli Schlanger who helped organize the event.

A Holocaust survivor named Alex Kleytman died while shielding his wife. A 10-year-old girl was also killed.

Ahmed Al-Ahmad, a 43-year-old Syrian-Australian fruit seller, hid behind a parked car.

He told his cousin, "I'm going to die," but then ran at the shooter anyway.

He wrestled away a rifle but got shot 5 times by the second gunman. One bullet is still in his shoulder.

He might lose his arm but said he would do it again.

Later, in the hospital, the brother-in-law of the murdered Rabbi Schlanger visited Ahmed.

He said, "Thank you for your courage. The fact that you come from a Muslim background rather than a Jewish one is special."

Ahmed replied: "No matter what happens, we are all human beings, and no matter what religion, we must be together and save lives."

His father, who escaped Syria and reunited with him in Australia this year, said Ahmed acted because of his "conscience and soul."

Bill Ackman donated $99,999 – the highest amount allowed on GoFundMe. More than $1.65 million was raised in total.

The Prime Minister visited him. Trump called him "very, very brave." Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu praised him.

Muslim leaders in Sydney said they would not accept the terrorist's body or hold Islamic burial rites. This was a full rejection.

This story shows courage beyond religion.

The attackers were a father-son pair who went to the Philippines last month for military-style training with possible ISIS links. The father was killed at the scene. The son is in hospital and faces charges.

Australia's worst mass shooting in decades showed that courage does not depend on religion.

People giving money for Ahmed's recovery are honoring a man who risked his life for others.

Sometimes, humanity wins. This was one of those times.

Sources: https://t.co/QvRwu4gLEq, CBS News, Al Jazeera, ABC News, Times of Israel, @JewishWarrior13

The business owners who make the most money from SEO are the ones who are absolutely ruthless about speed to lead. 

Let me explain what I mean. 

Someone searches "emergency plumber near me" at 11pm because their basement is flooding. They click on the first three results in Google and call all of them. 

The plumber who answers first gets the job. It's that simple. 

If you let calls go to voicemail, if you take 2 hours to call back, if you rely on a VA in the Philippines to answer your phone, you're cooked. 

Your competition is going to eat your lunch. I have clients who get 100 calls a month from Google and close 40 jobs. I have other clients who get 100 calls a month and close 8 jobs. 

The difference isn't their service quality. It's not their pricing. 

It's their response time and sales process. 

The winners have someone competent answering the phone immediately. 

They know how to qualify a lead. They're confident and professional. They follow up aggressively. The losers have a 19 year old receptionist who doesn't give a shit and takes messages. 

If you're going to invest in SEO, you better be ready to handle the leads properly. 

Otherwise you're paying to generate leads that your competition ends up closing.
